summary: Tested the new Student 360 View feature end-to-end. Backend: created /app/backend/tests/test_student_360.py (13 pytest tests) covering GET /api/students/{id}/360 payload structure, stats, timeline newest-first ordering, notes CRUD (create->persist->delete, empty content 400, unknown note 404, ordering), AI insight generate + cache, and access control (404 unknown student, 401 unauthenticated, 403 for another teacher's student incl. notes/insight endpoints). All 13 passed. Frontend: verified all three entry points (Classes, Gradebook, Attendance) navigate to /students/{id} via student-360-link-{id}, back button (navigate(-1)) returns to the originating page in each case, direct URL load works, overview cards + timeline render, note add/delete works with input clearing and disabled-empty state, and AI insight regeneration returned 1260-char markdown in ~15s. Invalid student id renders the 'Student not found' fallback with a working back button.

issues: Delete-note button uses 'opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100' so it is completely unreachable/invisible on touch devices (no hover). Suggest md:opacity-0 md:group-hover:opacity-100 or always-visible low-contrast icon plus focus-visible:opacity-100.

Test data (Maria Garcia) has no attendance sessions and assignments without due dates, so timeline only showed 3 events (2 grades + 1 note) and Attendance Rate/Missing = '—'/0. Attendance and assignment_due timeline branches were only verified by code reading, not by rendered data. Recommend seeding attendance + due-dated assignments for a fuller visual check.

action_items: Optional: make note delete button reachable on touch/keyboard (hover-only opacity).
Optional: seed a student with attendance records + due-dated assignments to visually validate attendance/assignment_due timeline entries and attendance-rate card.
critical_code_review_comments: DELETE /api/students/{id}/notes/{note_id} skips _get_student_with_access; it is safe because the query is scoped by teacher_id (verified: 404 for foreign/unknown notes), but adding the access check would keep error semantics consistent (403 vs 404).
Student360.js uses `${window.location.origin}/api` instead of process.env.REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL — consistent with the rest of the codebase, but breaks if frontend and backend origins ever differ.

Missing-assignment logic depends on a[due_date] string comparison with today's UTC date; assignments without due_date are never counted as missing (matches observed 0 missing despite 5 ungraded assignments) — confirm this is intended.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of tested flows (3 entry points, back button, notes CRUD, AI insight, invalid id)

seed_data_creation: Temporary second teacher account (TEST_other_*@school.edu) + TEST class/student created and deleted within the 403 access-control test; TEST_ notes created and deleted during tests. No residual data expected.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Student 360 backend regression suite: /app/backend/tests/test_student_360.py (run with `cd /app/backend && pytest tests/test_student_360.py -v`). Known good data: student_40da2916 (Maria Garcia) in class_d79a6790, 2 grades, no attendance sessions. Classes page requires clicking a class card first before student-360 links appear (back button then returns to /classes/{class_id}, which is correct navigate(-1) behavior).
rca_of_the_issue: No defects found. Two initial test failures were my own payload errors (class create requires 'section'; students are created via POST /api/classes/{class_id}/students, not POST /api/students) and were fixed in the test file.
